title: Defence minister 'very concerned' after Poilievre claims constituent's job was threatened
summary: Defence Minister David McGuinty says he's asked his deputy to raise concerns about a Wainwright, Alta., nurse's job being threatened after she was photographed with Conservative Leader Pierre…

image.caption: Minister of National Defence David McGuinty, left, and deputy minister Christiane Fox prepare to appear at the defence committee on Thursday, where McGuinty commented on Poilievre's point of privilege. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

Defence Minister David McGuinty says he's asked his deputy to raise concerns about a Wainwright, Alta., nurse's job being threatened after she was photographed with Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre.
Poilievre said nurse scrutinized for photo with Conservative leader after Wainwright fire

The minister told MPs on the House defence committee that the issue was brought up with the government contractor that employs the nurse, but beyond that there is little more that he could do at this point.

"This is a matter of privity of contract between her and her employer, which is a contractor to the federal government. So obviously you can imagine I can't involve myself in that private sector contract," he said.
"I did ask my deputy to speak to the company involved to at least raise the issue. It was raised."
This photo of nurse Maureen Carpenter was posted online by Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre on Oct. 20. (Pierre Poilievre/Facebook)
In an unusual speech in the House of Commons on Wednesday evening, Poilievre said his parliamentary privilege is being breached because of the incident.

Last month, Maureen Carpenter — a nurse who helped treat soldiers burned in the CFB Wainwright fire — was photographed speaking to Poilievre following the tragic incident that killed five soldiers and wounded 38 others on Oct. 17. Poilievre said she is under contract with Calian Health, a government contractor.

"Maureen spoke to me on base, with the permission of the unit commander. I had the permission of the base commander to be there. She talked about caring for our men and women on the shift that night, that horrendous night," said Poilievre.

items: Poilievre claims constituent's job was threatened after meeting at CFB Wainwright

blocks.text: An online post from Oct. 20 shows Poilievre meeting with medical staff at CFB Wainwright Health Services. Online comments identify the woman in the photo as Carpenter, which was confirmed by Poilievre's office.
The base is part of Poilievre's federal riding of Battle River-Crowfoot.

He said, following the meeting, Carpenter was subject to a complaint and threatened — told by her boss that if her term contract was not already coming to an end, she would be put under the microscope by the company's legal department.
McGuinty said during the committee meeting that he agrees with Poilievre "that constituents should always feel free — and MPs should always be able to speak to their constituents."
"I've been on this file, on this issue, because I'm very concerned. It's not right that a member of Parliament should not be able to speak to a constituent."
Now that Poilievre has raised the matter as a point of privilege, the minister said he needs to wait for the Speaker's ruling as well.

"I can't cross a certain other line, which is the question of now this claim that Mr. Poilievre's own privileges have been affected. That's now residing with the Speaker and I'm hoping for a good outcome in terms of the decision there."
McGuinty said he has been in contact with Carpenter's brother.
CBC News has reached out to Calian Health and Carpenter for comment but has not yet received a response.
